thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Inch Higher As S&P 500 Tries For 4th Up Day In A Row

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Inch Higher As S&P 500 Tries For 4th Up Day In A Row
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Foreign central banks, Hurricane Florence likely to spark market moves
U.S. stock futures edged up Thursday, signaling the S&P 500 could gain for a fourth session in a row.
Investors are due to get a key reading on inflation, as well as a fresh figure for jobless claims. Foreign central banks and Hurricane Florence also are likely to spark market moves.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures tacked on 14 points, or 0.1% to 26,028, while S&P 500 futures added 1.35 points, or 0.1%, to 2,889.75. Nasdaq-100 futures rose by 7 points, or 0.1%, to 7,492.75.
On Wednesday, the Dow closed up by 0.1% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-inch-up-as-apples-iphone-event-grabs-the-spotlight-2018-09-12) and the S&P 500 gained less than 0.1%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.2%, as Apple Inc. shares (AAPL) lost 1.2% after the company unveiled new iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/everything-apple-just-announced-at-its-iphone-event-2018-09-12).
The Dow has risen for two days in a row, while the S&P has finished higher for three straight sessions. The three gauges have notched year-to-date gains of 5.2% to 15%, as of Wednesday's close.
What's driving markets?
Investors continue to track the trade-related tensions between the U.S. and China, the world's two largest economies.
There is some optimism after a report late Wednesday that the Trump administration is giving Beijing another chance (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-offers-renewed-trade-talks-with-china-to-avert-new-tariffs-2018-09-12) to try to stave off new tariffs on $200 billion in Chinese exports. A fresh round of trade talks could take place later this month.
Which economic reports are on tap?
An August report for a consumer price index is slated to hit at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, with economists polled by MarketWatch forecasting a rise of 0.3% for the headline number.
At that same time, investors are due to get weekly jobless claims, with 210,000 claims expected.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
Meanwhile, the European Central Bank, Bank of England and Turkey's central bank are set to announce policy decisions within an hour of each other on Thursday, between 7 a.m. and 8 a.m. Eastern U.S. Time. Europe's two most prominent central banks are expected to signal caution (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/what-to-watch-from-boe-ecb-turkeys-central-bank-2018-09-13), while Turkey's institution could act vigorously to tame soaring inflation.
Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic is due to speak about the economic outlook at an event in Jackson, Miss., at 1:15 p.m. Eastern.
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares in Kroger Co.(KR) look set for active trading as the grocery chain is among the companies expected to post earnings before the open.
Stock-market moves tied to Hurricane Florence (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hurricane-florence-could-bring-catastrophic-flash-flooding-to-carolinas-virginia-2018-09-12) are likely to continue Thursday. Bojangles' Inc.(BOJA) has lost 7.9% this week as it's expected to be among the hardest-hit restaurant chains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/restaurant-companies-at-greatest-risk-as-hurricane-florence-bears-down-2018-09-11), while retailer Home Depot Inc. shares (HD) have gained 5.6%.
(END) 06:13 ET (10:13
